newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's sets programme to tackle millennium bug.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's sets programme to tackle millennium bug.

text.p: Dealing with the 'millennium bug' could cost Lloyd's of London 40 million stg over the next three years, a spokesman for the insurance market said on Wednesday.
And the spokesman would not rule out taking sanctions against members who failed to take the necessary steps to combat the problem.
The difficulties stem from computers using two digits to show the year.
Programmers originally used the system to save scarce processing capacity but at the turn of the century many computers will show 00 for the year and interpret it as 1900, potentially causing havoc.
Lloyd's is hosting a seminar on Thursday to raise awareness of the issue at Lloyd's amongst underwriters and brokers.

It has established a "Year 2000 Programme" to ensure firms are fully prepared and to provide central co-ordination of plans and activities, technical and legal guidelines and the sharing of information throughout Lloyd's.
A target of the end of 1998 has been set to address the issue.

Mike Taylor, managing director of Lloyd's insurance services was reluctant to specify the sanctions which may apply should members fail to take steps to meet the deadline but said they would be an obvious option for Lloyd's.
One difficulty is that Lloyd's has to define what 'compliance' with the programme entails. That issue will be taken up in coming months.

The estimated cost of 40 million stg was, said Taylor, imprecise and could not be validated before they had more information. Lloyd's hopes to complete the first steps in its programme including costing by September.
The development of specific plans and testing of results will take place through 1998.
